static_traits.name: Chen Cody
static_traits.family_status: Lives with spouse and a black Labrador
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems in the past; has not yet received psychotherapy; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to identify and articulate automatic thoughts, good cooperativeness, willing to try different perspectives and reframing

basic_info.main_problem: Worries about being seen as a 'hick' by others because of one's musical tastes and hobbies (such as country music, fishing, hunting), developing insecurity and Self-doubt, feeling shame and embarrassment almost daily in social situations or when discussing interests.
basic_info.core_demands: Decided to seek counseling when these feelings of inadequacy began affecting self-confidence and the relationship with one's spouse, hoping to improve confidence and interpersonal interaction.
growth_experiences: Feelings of being judged and insecurity began and intensified after marrying two years ago: post-marriage adjustment pressure made one care more about others' views of one's interests and identity, gradually developing into almost daily shame and embarrassment in social situations (such as gatherings, discussing hobbies); tried avoiding discussing interests to escape judgment, but this has not yet eased the underlying insecurity and Self-doubt.

core_beliefs: I am not respectable enough, others will treat me as a 'hick'.
My interests make people look down on me, I am not accepted.

special_situations.event: At last week's gathering, when asked about hobbies, the other person's reaction after fishing was mentioned made one feel looked down upon
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I talk about country music, fishing, or hunting, others will think I am uncultured, a 'hick'.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids continuing to talk about interests, stays quiet to avoid being judged.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They must think I am an uncultured 'hick'.

special_situations.event: In social interactions with colleagues involving interests or self-expression
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Exposing real interests in the workplace will be looked down on by colleagues, thereby affecting interpersonal evaluation and relationships.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Hiding one's interests in front of colleagues, avoiding related topics as much as possible.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Colleagues will think I am unprofessional and look down on me.

special_situations.event: Daily socializing and interaction with spouse under marital adaptation pressure
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others do not approve of my interests, it will harm intimate relationships, It is all my fault.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-censors and reduces expressing real interests to lower conflict and judgment.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My interests are making our relationship worse; it is my problem.

special_situations.event: When asked about interests or talking about hobbies in any situation
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only by staying quiet and not revealing one's true self is one safe.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should stay quiet and not show my true self.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be accepted and respected, able to freely express genuine interests without being shamed.
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being shamed, looked down upon, and rejected, thereby affecting intimate relationships and social standing.
defense_goal: Reducing external judgment through avoidance and self-Repression, maintaining superficial safety and relationship stability

object_relations.self_representation: The low-status person who is judged and shamed (worries about being a 'country bumpkin')
object_relations.object_representation: A contemptuous judge (others will look down on me)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked about interests or when country music, fishing, hunting, etc. are mentioned in social settings
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others will look down on me like a contemptuous judge (transference: projecting one's inner Negative self-evaluation onto others' reactions)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Avoid answering directly, use vague and self-deprecating statements, quickly shift the topic; keep a cautious tone, reduce self-disclosure.

manifestations: Repressing genuine interests and expression in Social situations to avoid judgment
Self-censoring, 'I should stay quiet and not show my true self'
outcomes: Interpersonal relationships damaged (interactions with spouse and colleagues affected)

manifestations: Although having a supportive spouse and friends, has not yet discussed the specific insecurity and feelings of being judged with them
Feeling looked down upon and isolated in Social situations
outcomes: Avoids communication, making it hard for support to take effect
Daily experiences of shame and embarrassment

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: At gatherings, believing the other person 'looks down on me' even without solid evidence
When interacting with colleagues, assuming others will find one unprofessional

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'. Language manifestations include: 'Forget it, I will just endure it', 'I should not trouble others', and so on
manifestations: Avoiding discussing interests, Suppressing expression of one's true self
Self-blame and the inner dialogue 'I should keep quiet'

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on
manifestations: Overly cautious in socializing, worried about being judged and shrinking expression

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'. Language manifestations include: 'Speaking of which... haha, just kidding', 'In theory...', and so on
manifestations: Shifting the topic or responding vaguely when asked about interests
Avoiding discussing specific insecurities with spouse and friends

exception_events.target_problem: When asked about interests in Social situations, the client typically worries about being looked down upon and avoids discussing them, then develops shame and insecurity that affect interaction.
exception_events.unique_outcome: When talking with a like-minded friend about hunting and fishing, the other party always responded enthusiastically and joined the activities together, making the client feel accepted and understood rather than judged.
exception_events.reason: Different support and context: the other person shares the client's interests, giving positive feedback and engagement; a like-minded environment lowers judgment risk and strengthens feelings of acceptance and confidence.

positive_force: Has a supportive spouse and several close friends to confide in
When interacting with fellow enthusiasts, can feel accepted (friends hunting or fishing together)
Work performance is stable; has basic functioning and a sense of responsibility
negative_force: Tends toward mind-reading and catastrophizing Anticipation of others' evaluations
Personalizing Relationship tension by attributing it to one's own interests and problems
Avoiding expressing genuine interests, Repression of self leading to Reduced self-consistency
Self-criticism and shame are frequent, weakening confidence and interpersonal interaction

target_behavior.behavior: In social situations, avoids talking about interests and hobbies
antecedent: At gatherings or occasions where one is asked about interests (for example, last week's gathering)
When conversations with colleagues touch on personal interests
Talking about hobbies when interacting with spouse
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing being looked down upon and labeled a 'hick'; influenced by post-marriage adjustment pressure, becoming more sensitive to others' evaluations and forming mind-reading and overgeneralizing cognitions.
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potential negative evaluation and shame experiences, maintaining surface safety and relationship stability.
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased self-confidence, Impaired interpersonal interaction, relationship with spouse affected; daily shame and embarrassment, difficulty expressing one's true self.

target_behavior.behavior: Self-deprecation and negative self-talk (such as 'I should stay quiet and not show my true self')
antecedent: Feeling others' reactions are unfriendly or uncomprehending when discussing interests
Becomes wary of others' gazes and questions in social settings
target_behavior.core_reason: The core belief 'I am not accepted, others will look down on me' drives Self-monitoring and coping; fearing humiliation and rejection.
target_behavior.function: Reducing exposure and judgment risk through self-Repression, lowering Anxiety in the short term.
target_behavior.consequence: Reinforcement of shame and insecurity, further weakening self-worth and interpersonal connections, affecting relationships with spouse and colleagues.
